intro:
Binh Gia and the coastal approaches — 28 December 1964

Comrade Commander, the fighting around Binh Gia is drawing South Vietnamese forces into the countryside east of Saigon. Local knowledge and surprise give our troops an opening before the government can concentrate its reserves.

In this scenario, strike the marked positions at Long Hai and Vung Tau. The purpose is to break the local defensive network and force the enemy to respond on ground of our choosing.

Keep the assault groups close enough to support one another and watch the roads behind the first objectives. A successful raid can quickly become an encirclement if the government troops arrive while our force is scattered across the coast.

intro:
Escape from Vung Tau — 29 December 1964

The raid has brought a response. South Vietnamese troops are moving to clear the coastal area, and our units must regain the jungle routes before the enemy closes them.

Bring at least five units out through the marked escape hexes. Cover the withdrawal with a rearguard and keep the slowest troops moving before the main roads are blocked. The crash site in this scenario may draw additional enemy attention; do not let it distract you from saving the force.

An alternative is to hold two victory objectives until the turn limit for a Brilliant Victory. Holding only one does not meet that threshold. Decide whether you have the strength to defend the positions or should concentrate on evacuation.

My orders are to tell you that Hanoi has decided that you and your command will be included into the North Vietnam Army.  Congratulations, you have been appointed the commander of this army.

intro:
Plei Me — 19 October 1965

The Special Forces camp at Plei Me supports government control of the Central Highlands and threatens the routes our troops use near Pleiku. Its local garrison has outside support close enough to make a prolonged attack dangerous.

Split the effort carefully: one group blocks the road and secures the northern objectives while the other attacks the camp. The defenders include locally recruited troops and American advisers; expect a relief effort and aircraft once the battle is under way.

Hold three victory objectives at the turn limit for a Brilliant Victory, two for a Victory, or one for a Tactical Victory. Taking the camp alone is not the whole operation. Keep the blocking force supplied and able to resist the relief column.

Most importantly you have unexpectedly beaten the imperialist invaders too. This is even sweeter given they were equipped with the very latest technology such us their helicopters. Now you should disappear quickly into the jungle before the Americans arrive again to claim revenge!.

intro:
Ia Drang — 14 November 1965

American helicopter-borne troops are establishing landing zones near our routes through the Central Highlands. Their mobility lets them appear beyond a normal front line, but each landing still depends on a patch of ground that can be held and supplied.

Clear the marked landing zones, including X-Ray and Albany, and take the other objectives. Local forces support the attack, while American artillery and aircraft can reach troops caught in the open.

Use the jungle to assemble the assault groups, keep them connected and watch for new landings behind them. The purpose is to deny the enemy secure bases from which to search the border country, not to gather the whole force under his supporting fire.

intro:
Cu Chi: preserve the local force — 4 January 1966

An enemy clearing operation is approaching the Cu Chi area. Our local units know the villages and supply routes; losing them would damage the organisation long after this battle is over.

Cover a withdrawal towards War Zone C and evacuate eight units through the marked exits. Move the local detachments early, use the stronger formations as a rearguard and avoid being pinned against the remaining roads.

The map also offers a Brilliant Victory for holding one objective to the turn limit. Preserving the local units is the narrative priority, but this version has no separate automatic defeat condition for losing a particular local unit. Choose between the defensive opportunity and the evacuation without leaving half the force committed to each.

briliant.text:

They are preparing their former positions for the return of our troops there.

Hanoi wants to celebrate your victory by moving your troops to a quiet place to give you and your men a rest.

intro:
Tuy Hoa — 18 July 1967

South Korean troops are preparing to clear our positions around Tuy Hoa. Their operation threatens the bases and routes from which local forces can return to the coastal districts.

Defend the marked objectives and use the terrain to keep the enemy from separating your detachments. Pull exposed units back towards a position they can hold together before the approaches are blocked; this scenario has no unit-evacuation quota.

At the turn limit, four objectives earn a Brilliant Victory, three a Victory and two a Tactical Victory. PAVN formations are available to strengthen your force as resources allow. Put that strength where it can support the local defenders rather than leaving it on an isolated stretch of the line.

briliant.text: Tot cong viec general!, with meager resources you have achieved all the objectives.  For now our supply routes through Laos and Cambodia are safe.

intro:
Kontum outposts — 3 November 1967

Government outposts in Kontum province overlook the routes that connect our border bases with the interior. An enemy offensive is expected, and those camps would give it places to assemble and resupply.

Attack the marked positions around Dak Pek, Dak Seang, Dak To and Kontum. Isolate the outposts before assaulting them, and keep a force ready to meet troops arriving to relieve a garrison.

Hold five objectives at the turn limit for a Brilliant Victory, four for a Victory, or three for a Tactical Victory. A camp captured and abandoned does not secure the route. Bring enough infantry forward to hold each position while the next attack is prepared.

intro:
Khe Sanh — 15 January 1968

The American combat base at Khe Sanh lies near Route 9 and the Laotian border. Its airstrip and hill positions allow the defenders to watch the approaches to an important part of our supply network.

Clear the marked hills, attack the combat base and its airstrip, and take Lang Vei and the remaining objectives. Reinforcements are approaching, but the enemy can use artillery and air power even when his ground routes are threatened.

Bring support weapons into position before exposing the assault groups. The base is a fortified military outpost, not a provincial capital, and reaching its perimeter will only begin the hardest part of the fighting.

intro:
Tet offensive: Hue and Da Nang — 31 January 1968

The Tet offensive seeks to bring the war into the cities and disrupt the South Vietnamese command system. Surprise may give the first attacking groups an opening, but government and American forces can respond quickly once the alarm is raised.

One part of your force attacks Hue, where the ARVN First Division headquarters and the American advisory compound are key centres of resistance. The other attacks the Da Nang area. Use the supporting rocket batteries to assist the assaults and keep routes open between captured positions.

Hold five marked objectives at the turn limit for a Brilliant Victory, four for a Victory, or two for a Tactical Victory. Entering a city is not the same as holding it against the counterattack.

intro:
Laos counteroffensive — 12 February 1971

South Vietnamese forces have entered Laos along Route 9, supported by American aircraft and helicopters. Their aim is to disrupt the supply system linking the northern bases with the war in the south.

Drive them out of the Xe Pon valley. Capture the marked firebases and landing sites, secure Tchepone and Route 9, and deny the enemy safe positions from which to continue the operation.

Our forces now have heavier weapons, but enemy air support remains dangerous. Use the jungle and hills to approach the isolated bases, then concentrate before attacking. Prevent the defenders from rescuing one threatened position while our assault groups are scattered around several others.

intro:
Kontum — 15 May 1972

The offensive has returned to the Central Highlands. South Vietnamese forces now carry the main burden of ground defence, with American advisers and powerful American air support still helping them.

Break the chain of marked firebases and take Kontum. Regional units support the advance, and anti-aircraft positions can help cover the attack, but they do not make a massed column safe from air strikes.

Use artillery against the strongpoints, keep the approaches under observation and move the assault troops from cover to cover. Kontum anchors the government position in this sector; taking its outer bases without reaching the city leaves that position incomplete.

intro:
Saigon — 24 April 1975

The South Vietnamese position is collapsing after the loss of the northern provinces and the Central Highlands. Surviving ARVN formations are falling back on the approaches to Saigon while the government tries to hold its remaining centres of command.

Capture the marked objectives around the capital, including Bien Hoa and the Saigon sectors, and clear the remaining resistance on the routes towards the coast. Concentrate the main effort so the defenders cannot defeat isolated columns at the outer strongpoints.

This is the final campaign operation. Take the capital and its communications centres before the defence can be reorganised. A Tactical Victory does not complete this campaign successfully; keep the displayed victory deadlines in view while bringing the infantry and guns forward.

Congratulations general, Saigon has been liberated! The Viet Cong flag has been raised over Independence Palace. The South Vietnam general Doung Van Minh has surrendered to us. The city will soon be renamed after our great leader Ho Chi Minh... It's time to inspect the US Embassy...
